At the edge of the harbor, the old lighthouse kept watch over a sea that had stopped needing it.

Ships carried maps, radios, satellites. The lighthouse had a cracked window and a gull’s nest in its crown. Still, every evening, the keeper climbed the spiral stairs and lit the lamp.

“Someone might be lost,” he said.

One night, a child came down to the water’s edge with a paper boat. She set it afloat, and the tide took it past the rocks and out into the dark. The lighthouse turned its bright eye across the waves.

The child watched until the beam swept back to shore.

“See?” said the keeper. “Not everything lost is far away.”
